content.title: CIME Nairobi becomes the first in AKU to introduce an automated system to manage OSCEs
content.summary: The 12 rooms Assessment and Communication suite in CIME Nairobi is now fully equipped with the B-line Medical Debriefing System.

media.alt: CIME Nairobi becomes the first in AKU to introduce an automated system to manage OSCEs

content.text: The 12 rooms Assessment and Communication suite in CIME Nairobi is now fully equipped with the B-line Medical Debriefing System. This advance system provides faculty and staff with a one-window solution in planning, managing, and evaluating student performance during simulated practice and Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs). With this implementation, CIME Nairobi becomes the first to introduce an automated system throughout AKU global campuses to manage OSCEs.

The system allows faculty to work from a distance while still being able to evaluate student performance in an OSCE at their convenience, reducing the time and effort required by administrators to plan OSCEs. A control room present within the suite, allows technical and administrative staff to observe and provide support when required. With video recording, evidence of student performance can be shared with external evaluators and the students themselves to improve transparency of the process.
